Before you apply for a student loan, we need to make sure you meet the following requirements.

**To apply:**

- You need to already have a Bank of Ireland 3rd level personal current account

- You need to be studying at a college approved by the CAO (Central Applications Office)

fields.label: Before you apply for a top up...
fields.content:
# Getting started

Before you apply for a top up, we need to check that you're happy with a few things.

When you borrow more, we close your existing loan and open a new one. The new loan will include your remaining balance, any interest owed, and your top up amount.

**To apply you need:**
- An existing Bank of Ireland loan
- At least 6 months' payments on your loan
- All your payments up-to-date
- To know the current balance of the loan you want to top up. If you have already added your loan account to your 365 online profile, you can check your most recent balance through the BOI app. 

[How do I add my existing loan account to my 365 online profile?](https://www.bankofireland.com/help-centre/faq/can-add-accounts-view-365-online/#tabpanel_1)

# Let’s Get Started

fields.label: Forgot your 365 online User ID
fields.content:
**Forgot your 365 online User ID?**

If you’ve forgotten your User ID, **free text** the word ‘User’ to 50365 and we’ll reply with your user ID within seconds.

**If you have an account with us but are not yet activated for online banking, you’ll need to follow these steps:**

fields.label: Steps
fields.content:
**Step 1:** Call us on [0818 214 365](tel:+353818214365) to activate your account. You will need your account number available.

**Step 2:** To protect the privacy on your account we will ask you to verify your identity.

**Step 3:** We will instruct you on how to set up your own unique PIN and will then send you your user ID by text. 

**Step 4:** You can then activate your account and start banking online straight away – after that, just come back to continue your application.

- Online if you filed your income tax return on the revenue website
- By post if you filed your income tax return using the paper form
- From your accountant if they filed your income tax return on your behalf

fields.description:
**How do I know if I have received State aid in the past?**   
State aid can occur when State resources are provided to entities or persons engaged in economic activities, thereby creating an advantage over others by virtue of benefiting from those State resources. The maximum amount of De Minimis State aid a single recipient can receive is EUR 300,000 in the previous three-year period. If you have received De Minimis State aid in the last 3 years, you should have received a State aid letter notifying you of the amount of State aid received. State aid can be received in the form of grants, guarantees or subsidized loans. Examples of sources of State aid are Enterprise Ireland, Local Enterprise Offices, the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland, the Strategic Banking Corporation of Ireland or the Environmental Protection Agency. [For further information on De Minimis State aid please refer to the SBCI website](https://sbci.gov.ie/about-us/regulation)

fields.label: Credit Reporting Act 2013 - Warning Box
fields.content: **NOTICE: Under the Credit Reporting Act 2013 lenders are required to provide personal and credit information for credit applications and credit agreements of €500 and above to the Central Credit Register. This information will be held on the Central Credit Register and may be used by other lenders when making decisions on your credit applications and credit agreements.**

fields.label: The Central Credit Register is owned and operated by the Central Bank of Ireland.
fields.content: The Central Credit Register is owned and operated by the Central Bank of Ireland. [For more information, including on how your data is processed, visit the Central Credit Register website](https://www.centralcreditregister.ie/).

fields.label: Accordion
fields.accordion_content:
You are entitled to:
- get a copy of your credit record from the Central Bank (you can order one free copy per year).
- correct any errors on your credit record.
- tell the Central Bank if you suspect you may have been impersonated.
- ask the Central Bank to add a short explanation written by you to your credit record.

fields.label: Credit Reference Agencies
fields.content:
**Credit Reference Agencies**

As part of the application process and ongoing loan management, we will carry out credit checks and share information with the Central Credit Register (CCR) and/or other credit reference agencies.

Those agencies may keep a record of this information and may give it to other financial institutions that you apply to for credit facilities.
